title: Choose the visual world for Online Shop
question: One direction leads. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Season Line
options.lineage: Seoul subway line maps and station signage
options.thesis: The store is a metro map: four season lines, categories are stations, every product has a stop.
options.viewport: A white platform sign bearing the current season line, a giant cutout product on its stop marker, the LED board scrolling as the marquee, and an add-to-cart that sits on the sign.
options.risk: Wayfinding can read cool and civic; the doodles and full line-colour floods must carry the youth, or it becomes a transit authority.

raised.raise: Choosing a season floods the header, buttons and marquee with that line's colour, the way a team livery floods a readout.
Full traceability: every card and product page shows its line, station and a 'Made in Korea' origin stop.
One reserved state mark: the 'you are here' dot appears only on the current location or selection.
Doodles in one ink and one stroke weight across the store, never multicolour clip art.
Product cards are identical modules that line up like stations on one ruler.
Route changes run as one orchestrated platform-door wipe instead of scattered hover effects.

options.label: Deco Diary
options.thesis: The store as a decorated planner: products are die-cut stickers, seasons are planner tabs.
options.viewport: A grid-paper spread with a huge sticker-cut product, washi-taped price tag and season tabs down the edge.
options.risk: Stickers and doodles are where most youthful shop designs land; familiar and effective rather than distinct.

options.label: Racing League Livery
options.thesis: Products as liveried craft, seasons as teams.
options.viewport: A liveried product streaking left to right.
options.case: Loses both axes: racing has no tie to Korean imports, and invented sponsor decals invite fake claims.
options.risk: Fabricated sponsors erode the authenticity promise.
options.kept: Selection floods the interface with the chosen colour.

options.label: Jacquard Brocade
options.thesis: Every product woven from traceable thread decisions.
options.viewport: A gold motif resolving over silk.
options.case: Loses both axes: luxury silk is not youthful, and the loom metaphor hides prices.
options.risk: Reads luxury-heritage, the opposite of the brief.
options.kept: Full traceability from collection to single item.

options.label: Accretion Disk
options.viewport: A glowing disk around a dark centre.
options.case: Loses both axes: no shopper link, and darkness fights clear prices on phones.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the active state only.

options.label: Penny Broadside
options.thesis: Each drop shouted as the day's sheet.
options.viewport: A wood-type headline over an engraving band.
options.case: Loses both axes: the imagery belongs to another culture, and dense verse slows mobile shopping.
options.risk: Cultural mismatch for a Korean-modern store.
options.kept: One ink, one line weight for every drawn mark.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Products as channels on one bridge.
options.viewport: A row of needles leaning into the red.
options.case: Loses both axes: studio gear is not this audience's world, and meters say nothing about products.
options.kept: Identical units repeating as the row's ruler.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A living shader with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: One hero word over moving pixels.
options.case: Loses both axes: heavy for phones in Mongolia, and hides the products.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean fashion-and-home store template, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Announcement bar, logo and menu, full-width banner, category tiles, product grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other shops by design.
